clue.text: Since all have indubitably been seated, the gents want their starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters, so the first letter of each of the six words in the long opening phrase is taken

explanation.surface: Once everyone has sat down, the gentlemen are keen to be served their first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like the first course of the meal in the picture; it actually tells you to take the initial letters of 'Since all have indubitably been seated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was the respectful title for a European gentleman in colonial India, so sahibs are gentlemen.

clue.text: A base got destroyed by enemy action

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters of the three words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A military base was wrecked in an attack by the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or obstruction carried out by enemies or agents.

clue.text: Doctor recited poems from, his pen

indicators.note: recited means spoken aloud, so we want a name pronounced the same as the doctor's title

parts.note: a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain

explanation.surface: A physician read out verses he had written himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is the British term for a newly qualified doctor working in a hospital, roughly an intern.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Housman wrote the poetry collection A Shropshire Lad, so poems came from his pen.

clue.text: Taps, perhaps, irritate the French on occasion

parts.note: to bug someone is to annoy them
le is French for the
call means occasion or reason, as in no call to worry

explanation.surface: Tapping, now and then, gets on French people's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taps' looks like tapping noises; it is the US military bugle call played at lights-out and funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Taps is the bugle signal sounded at military funerals and for lights out, one example of a call played on a bugle.

clue.text: Don discovers well about empty. .

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for empty is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to drain a vessel is to empty it

explanation.surface: A university don finds a well that has dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university lecturer; it is the Spanish courtesy title for a gentleman, standing for any man of Spain. 'about' reverses the word for empty to give NIARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is the Spanish honorific for a gentleman, so a don is a man of Spain.

clue.text: Celebrate launch

definitions.meaning: to spend lavishly on a festive occasion
literally to shove a vessel off into the water

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to splash out on a celebration, and literally describes pushing a vessel into the water to launch it.

clue.text: Republic put up with the loss of an explosives expert

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from bottom to top, so the letters are read backwards
with the loss of means minus, so the two letters are removed

parts.note: Lebanon is a republic in the Middle East
taken as written

explanation.surface: A republic tolerated the death of a man who made bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republic' is the definition's decoy: it is the country, and the inventor is defined by 'explosives expert'. In a down clue 'put up' reads the shortened country, LEBON, upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who founded the prizes, invented dynamite.

clue.text: Starting in rags; I get tidied up

indicators.note: tidied up means rearranged into order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone in shabby clothes begins smartening up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' looks like a description of the person beginning; it is the definition, meaning coming into being.
explanation.definitionFit: Arising means coming into existence or emerging, as a problem arising is one beginning to appear.

clue.text: Unemployment makes entertainer lose heart .

indicators.note: lose heart means drop the central letter of the entertainer's word

parts.note: a diseuse is a female performer who gives dramatic monologues

explanation.surface: Being out of work causes a performer to become discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose heart' removes the middle E of DISEUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of not being employed or used, as of a machine left idle.

clue.text: Just like a papal blessing

definitions.meaning: exactly resembling, an idiom used as in 'she looked exactly like her mother'
the Pope's urbi et orbi blessing is addressed to the city and the whole globe

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in every respect, and the Pope's Easter blessing is given to the city and to everyone on earth.

clue.text: To show dissatisfaction about press is conventional

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jeering word goes round the word for press

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval
to press someone is to urge them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that grumbling about the press is merely the conventional thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourgeois describes middle-class values seen as conventional and unadventurous.

clue.text: Joy's music master

definitions.meaning: joy is happiness or delight; the 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions
Sir Arthur ..., the English composer, was Master of the Queen's Music from 1953

explanation.walkthrough: The Master of the Queen's (or King's) Music is the British court composer, an honorary royal post; Arthur Bliss held it from 1953 to 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is perfect happiness, and Arthur Bliss held the royal post of Master of the Queen's Music.

clue.text: Given backing, a theatre company gathered artistic technique

indicators.note: given backing means sent backwards, so the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: rep is short for a repertory theatre company
people who gathered met

explanation.surface: A theatre company, once sponsored, came together to learn a painting method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given backing' sounds like financial support for the company; it turns the whole run A + REP + MET backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a painting method using pigment bound in egg yolk, a technique of the visual arts.

clue.text: Matches. everyone held matches

indicators.note: held means contained, so the word for everyone sits inside the word for sporting fixtures

parts.note: ties are matches in a knockout competition, as in cup ties
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody was holding matchsticks.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'matches' do different jobs: the first is a verb meaning agrees, the second a noun meaning sporting fixtures. In British football a cup tie is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: When two figures correspond or agree, one is said to tally with the other.

clue.text: Sail from port

definitions.meaning: a large jib sail on a yacht
The major seaport of north-west Italy

explanation.surface: An instruction to set off by boat from a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The big foresail called a genoa takes its name from the Italian port city of Genoa.

clue.text: In dilapidated lodge I try to keep out of sight

indicators.note: dilapidated means broken down, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Someone hides away in a run-down hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodge' looks like the hiding place in the picture, but it is only fodder: 'dilapidated' reshuffles it with I to give LIEDOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is an informal idiom for staying hidden and quiet, like a dog playing dead.

clue.text: Worried re down-and-out royal / forebear

indicators.note: worried means shaken about like a dog with a bone, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Concern about a down-and-out member of the royal family's ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' rearranges RE, DOWN and OUT; 'and' is only the link in 'down-and-out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen Tudor, a Welsh courtier who married Henry V's widow, was grandfather of Henry VII and founder of the Tudor dynasty.

clue.text: Without any fuss, insert, some "old numbers into 'show

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the numerals go within the word for a stage show

parts.note: a play is a show staged in a theatre
C, I, D and L are Roman numerals, numbers of old

explanation.surface: Calmly adding a few vintage songs to a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old numbers' looks like old songs for the show; they are Roman numerals C, I, D and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something placidly is doing it calmly and peacefully, without agitation.

clue.text: Social function attended by lout putting out a lot of noisy publicity

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance, a social function

indicators.note: putting out means expelling, so the named letter is dropped from the word for lout

parts.note: a yahoo is a coarse, boorish person, from Swift's Gulliver's Travels
the letter A, given as written

explanation.surface: A society dance gatecrashed by a thug who throws people out makes headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out a' takes the A out of YAHOO, leaving YHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is sensational promotion or fuss, a great deal of loud advertising.

clue.text: Poison it's. concealed in an ice-cream

indicators.note: concealed in means hidden inside, so the word it goes within the ice-cream

parts.note: a cone is an ice-cream served in a wafer cone
it, with the 's standing for 'is'

explanation.surface: A deadly toxin was hidden in a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a plant whose roots yield a deadly toxin.

clue.text: Welsh — Welsh wanting to make a stand

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the abbreviation is removed from the verb for reneging

parts.note: to welsh on a debt is to weasel out of it

explanation.surface: A Welshman wants to take a stand on the matter of his nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Welsh' is the verb meaning go back on a promise, which WEASEL also means; the second gives its abbreviation W.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame or stand on which a painter's canvas rests.

clue.text: Start to shrivel if not shaded

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: unless means if not

explanation.surface: Plants begin to wither unless they are kept out of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaded place gets no direct sunlight.

clue.text: Husband latterly forgets to wave

indicators.note: latterly means at the end, so the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: to crimp hair is to wave or curl it

explanation.surface: A married man eventually forgets to wave goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is a verb meaning to use sparingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to manage them thriftily, as to scrimp is to economise.

clue.text: Step on ice — kind of ice melting though it's not hot inside

parts.note: a choc ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate, so choc is a kind of ice

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for hot is taken away
inside says the letter for hot is taken from the middle of the word for melting

parts.note: melting snow is in a thaw
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A skater's move on ice, compared with an ice cream that melts even without heat.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a bar of ice cream coated in chocolate, sold in Britain. Removing H from the middle of THAW leaves TAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A choctaw is a figure-skating movement from one edge of a skate to the opposite edge, changing foot.

clue.text: Nip the heart out of a shallot, some say

parts.note: a nip and a tot are both small measures of spirits

indicators.note: the heart out of means the central letters of the two words taken together

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut the core out of a small onion, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken: 'some', said aloud, is SUM, which means a total. The middle of 'a shallot' (ASHALLOT) is AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is a sum, and 'some' is pronounced exactly like sum.

clue.text: They said "It can't sink, can it?" — it foundered

indicators.note: foundered means sank or went wrong, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The ship was proclaimed unsinkable, yet it went down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundered' rearranges the letters of 'can it' and 'it' (CANITIT).
explanation.definitionFit: The liner launched in 1912 was famously claimed to be practically unsinkable before it struck an iceberg.

clue.text: I would love to be in it, but I'm too stupid

definitions.text: I would love to be in it, but I'm too stupid

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: to be in means placed within, so the zero goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
love is a zero score in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone longs to join in but admits they are not clever enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The speaker confesses to being too dim to take part, which is what a fool would say.

clue.text: Parliamentarian 'revealing nothing in a hundred different ways

indicators.note: arranged in different ways, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: nothing is zero, written O

explanation.surface: A member of parliament who gives nothing away in a hundred different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different ways' rearranges O and A HUNDRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads were supporters of Parliament against the King in the English Civil War, named for their cropped hair.

clue.text: Rule out use of a key in a piece of music

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter for the key goes within the musical piece

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece of music
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Disallowing the use of a certain key in a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent it or make it impossible from the outset.

clue.text: Frightful noise 'to bear

indicators.note: noise means the word is spoken, so we want something pronounced the same as the bear

parts.note: the grizzly is a large North American brown bear

explanation.surface: A dreadful sound that someone has to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' seems to be the verb endure; it is the animal, the grizzly.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisly means gruesome, causing horror or disgust.
